text: Christian Dior SE, commonly known as Dior, is a French multinational luxury goods company controlled and chaired by Bernard Arnault, who also leads LVMH. As of December 2023, Dior held approximately 42% of LVMH's shares and 57% of its voting rights, with the Arnault family owning an additional 7% of shares and 8% of voting rights. The original fashion house was founded by Christian Dior in 1946 at 30 Avenue Montaigne in Paris, though the company celebrates 1947 as its founding year. It was financially backed by Marcel Boussac, who had invited Dior to design for Philippe et Gaston, but Dior declined to revive an old brand and instead launched a new venture under his own name. The new couture house became part of Boussac’s vertically integrated textile business, with a capital of FFr 6 million and 80 employees. Despite Boussac’s reputation as a "control freak," Dior was granted significant autonomy, including legal leadership, a non-controlling stake, and one-third of pretax profits, along with a good salary. On 12 February 1947, Christian Dior launched his first collection for Spring–Summer 1947, presented in the salons of 30 Avenue Montaigne with 90 models on six mannequins. The collection, originally named "Corolle" and "Huit," became known as the "New Look" after Harper’s Bazaar editor Carmel Snow exclaimed, "It's such a new look!" and later called it "a revolution." The New Look featured a small nipped-in waist and full skirt to mid-calf, emphasizing the bust and hips, with the "Bar" suit designed by Pierre Cardin, who worked at Dior from 1947 to 1949. The style revived French haute couture, which had declined after World War II, and was embraced by Hollywood, European aristocracy, and figures like Princess Margaret. The New Look influenced fashion well into the 1950s and beyond, with designers such as Thom Browne, Miuccia Prada, and Vivienne Westwood citing its impact. However, some criticized the designs as wasteful and restrictive, especially feminists and groups like the League of Broke Husbands, which included 30,000 men. Coco Chanel remarked, "Only a man who never was intimate with a woman could design something that uncomfortable." Despite opposition, the New Look remained influential, with John Galliano revisiting it in 2007 and Raf Simons reinterpreting it in 2012 with a minimalist, sensual approach that emphasized self-respect and body liberation. Christian Dior Parfums was established in 1947 with the launch of Miss Dior, named after Christian’s sister Catherine, and was jointly owned by Christian Dior Ltd (25%), Coty (35%), and Boussac (40%). A New York branch opened in 1948, and the Diorama perfume was released in 1949, with the New Look line alone generating a profit of FFr 12.7 million that year. By the end of 1949, Dior fashions accounted for 75% of Paris’s fashion exports and 5% of France’s total export revenue. In 1949, Douglas Cox from Melbourne signed a contract with Dior to produce designs in Australia, but the avant-garde models were too radical for local tastes, ending the partnership after one season. In 1950, Jacques Rouët introduced a licensing program, first on neckties, then expanded to hosiery, furs, hats, gloves, handbags, jewelry, lingerie, and scarves, despite criticism from the French Chamber of Couture. Dior designed Marlene Dietrich’s dresses for the film Stage Fright in 1950 and released its first book, Je Suis Couturier, in 1951. By this time, over half of Dior’s revenue came from the United States. A Christian Dior Models Limited was established in London in 1952, and agreements were made with Sydney’s House of Youth and Los Gobelinos in Santiago, Chile. The first Dior shoe line was launched in 1953 with Roger Vivier, and by the end of 1953, Dior had established locations in Mexico, Cuba, Canada, and Italy. Counterfeiting grew as popularity increased. In 1954, the first Dior boutique opened at 9 Conduit Street, and a fashion show was held at Blenheim Palace in honor of Princess Margaret and the Duchess of Marlborough. Dior launched several successful lines between 1954 and 1957, though none matched the impact of the New Look. The Grande Boutique opened in 1955 on the corner of Avenue Montaigne and Rue François Ier, and the first Dior lipstick was released that year. By 1956, 100,000 garments had been sold, and actress Ava Gardner had 14 dresses made for the film The Little Hut. Christian Dior appeared on the cover of Time on 4 March 1957 and died from a third heart attack on 24 October 1957. His legacy as a fashion icon was cemented, with Kevin Almond noting that by his death, his name became synonymous with taste and luxury. Notable figures such as Jacqueline Kennedy, Elizabeth Taylor, Edith Piaf, and Marlene Dietrich wore his designs. After Dior’s death, the house faced chaos, and general manager Jacques Rouët considered shutting it down, but industry stakeholders prevented this. Rouët promoted 21-year-old Yves Saint Laurent as Artistic Director in 1958. Saint Laurent, who had joined Dior in 1955 as Head Assistant, created collections that were meticulously crafted and softer, lighter, and more wearable than Dior’s. His 1960 "Beat Look," inspired by existentialist cafés and jazz clubs, was criticized by Women’s Wear Daily and led to his forced departure when he was called up for military service in 1960. Saint Laurent completed six collections before leaving. He was replaced by Marc Bohan in late 1960, who introduced a conservative style and was credited with keeping Dior at the forefront of fashion while producing elegant, wearable clothing. Elizabeth Taylor ordered twelve dresses from Bohan’s 1961 Spring-Summer collection featuring the "Slim Look." Dior launched "Diorling" in 1963 and "Eau Sauvage" in 1966. Bohan’s assistant Philippe Guibourgé launched the first French ready-to-wear collection, "Miss Dior," in 1967, distinct from the 1948 New York ready-to-wear store. "Baby Dior" opened its first boutique in 1967 at 28 Avenue Montaigne. The Christian Dior Coordinated Knit line was introduced in 1968, and Frédéric Castet took over the Fashion Furs Department. In 1969, Dior Parfums was sold to Moët-Hennessy (which later became LVMH) due to Boussac’s failing textile business, but operations continued, and the Christian Dior Cosmetics business was launched that year. Bohan launched the first Christian Dior Monsieur (now Dior Men) line in 1970. A new boutique at Parly II was decorated by Gae Aulenti, and "Diorella" was released in 1972. The Christian Dior Ready-to-Wear Fur Collection was created in France in 1973 and manufactured under license in the U.S., Canada, and Japan. The first Dior watch, "Black Moon," was released in 1975 in collaboration with Benedom. Dior haute-couture was worn by First Lady Jacqueline Kennedy, Princess Grace of Monaco, Nicaraguan First Lady Hope Portocarrero, Princess Alexandra of Yugoslavia, and Lady Pamela Hicks at the wedding of Prince Charles and Lady Diana Spencer. In 1978, the Boussac Group filed for bankruptcy, and its assets—including Dior—were acquired by the Willot Group with Paris Trade Court approval. "Dioressence" was released in 1979, followed by "Jules" in 1980. After the Willot Group went bankrupt in 1981, Bernard Arnault and his investment group purchased it for "one symbolic franc" in December 1984. In 1985, Dior launched the "Poison" perfume, and Arnault became chairman, CEO, and managing director of the company. He eliminated the company’s mediocre textile operations, focusing instead on Bon Marché and Christian Dior Couture. Under his leadership, the company was repositioned as the holding company Christian Dior S.A.

The Boussac Group filed for bankruptcy in 1978, and its assets, including those of Christian Dior, were purchased by the Willot Group with permission from the Paris Trade Court. In 1979, the perfume "Dioressence" was released, followed by the men's fragrance "Jules" in 1980. After the Willot Group went bankrupt in 1981, Bernard Arnault and his investment group acquired it for "one symbolic franc" in December 1984. In 1985, the Dior perfume "Poison" was launched, and that same year, Arnault became chairman, chief executive officer, and managing director of the company. He eliminated the company's mediocre textile operations, repositioning Christian Dior as the holding company Christian Dior S.A. focused on Dior Couture fashion. On the 40th anniversary of Dior's first collection, the Paris Fashion Museum dedicated an exhibition to Christian Dior. In 1988, Christian Dior S.A. took a 32% equity stake in Moët-Hennessy • Louis Vuitton through its subsidiary Jacques Rober, uniting Christian Dior Couture and Christian Dior Parfums. In 1989, Italian-born Gianfranco Ferré replaced Bohan as head designer, becoming the first non-Frenchman in the role; his style was described as "refined, sober and strict," and his first collection won the Dé d'Or. That year, a boutique opened in Hawaii and the LVMH stake rose to 44%. In 1990, Dior boutiques opened in upscale New York City, Los Angeles, and Tokyo, and the stake in LVMH increased to 46%. The "Bagheera" watch collection, inspired by the "Black Moon" watches, was released in 1990. After firing managing executive Beatrice Bongbault in December 1990, Arnault took over the position until September 1991, when he appointed former Bon Marché president Phillipe Vindry. In 1991, Christian Dior was listed on the spot market and then on the Paris Stock Exchange's monthly settlement market, and the perfume "Dune" was launched. Vindry reduced ready-to-wear prices by 10%, though a wool suit still carried a price of USD 1,500. Dior's 1990 revenue was USD 129.3 million with a net income of $22 million. The company was reorganized into three categories: women's ready-to-wear, lingerie, and children's wear; accessories and jewelry; and menswear. Licensing was reduced by nearly half to emphasize quality and exclusivity over accessibility. Wholly owned boutiques opened in Hong Kong, Singapore, Kuala Lumpur, Cannes, and Waikiki, adding to core stores in New York City, Hawaii, Paris, and Geneva. In 1992, Dior Homme was placed under Patrick Lavoix, and the "Miss Dior" perfume was relaunched. Francois Baufume succeeded Vindry in 1993 and continued reducing licenses. In 1995, Dior Haute Couture was spun off into a subsidiary named Christian Dior Couture. The "La Parisienne" watch model, embodied in the "Parisian Chic" watch, was released. By that year, revenue reached USD 177 million with a net income of USD 26.9 million. In 1997, under Anna Wintour's influence, Arnault appointed British designer John Galliano to replace Gianfranco Ferré, a decision said to have "ruffled some French feathers," though Arnault stated he preferred a Frenchman but believed talent has no nationality. He compared Galliano to Christian Dior, noting his romanticism, feminism, and modernity. Galliano sparked controversy with fashion shows such as "Homeless Show" and "S&M Show." Meanwhile, Dior licenses were reduced under new CEO Sidney Toledano. On 15 October 1997, the Dior headquarters store on Avenue Montaigne was reopened after being closed and remodeled by Peter Marino, with a celebrity-studded event including Nicole Kidman, Demi Moore, and Jacques Chirac. That year, Christian Dior Couture took over all thirteen boutique franchises from Japan's Kanebo. In May 1998, a Dior boutique opened on the Left Bank of Paris at Place Saint-Germain-des-Prés. Victoire de Castellane became lead designer of Dior Fine Jewellery and opened the first Dior Fine Jewellery boutique in New York City; the first Parisian Dior Fine Jewellery boutique opened the following year at 28 Avenue Montaigne. The perfume "J'adore" was released in 1999. In October 1999, Galliano debuted the Dior Spring-Summer 2000 ready-to-wear show, introducing the iconic Dior Saddle bag, which became one of the first "It Bags" of the 2000s. The show reflected hip-hop's influence on luxury fashion, drawing inspiration from Lauryn Hill, and marked the rise of "logomania" as luxury brands embraced logo-heavy aesthetics. The show featured models in denim, monogram prints, and locs, blending streetwear with couture. In 1999, Dior's long watch partner Benedom joined the LVMH group. In 2000, Galliano's leadership expanded to ready-to-wear, accessories, advertising, and communications. His first campaign, photographed by Nick Knight, featured two women simulating intercourse, sparking a trend of suggestive advertising in fashion, similar to Gucci. Galliano is credited with revolutionizing Dior's advertising more than its designs. On 17 July 2000, Patrick Lavoix was replaced by Hedi Slimane as Dior Homme lead designer. Notable releases that year included the "Malice" watch with CD-link bracelets and the "Riva" watch. In 2001, Galliano launched the "Chris 47 Aluminum" watch line, followed by redesigned "Malice Sparkling" and "Riva Sparkling" collections with precious stones. Inspired by the Spring-Summer 2002 collection, the "Dior 66" watch was released, breaking traditional feminine design expectations. In 2001, the Dior Homme boutique on 30 Avenue Montaigne reopened with a "contemporary masculine concept" under Slimane, who later gained prominent male clients including Brad Pitt and Mick Jagger. The men's fragrance "Higher" was released in 2001, followed by "Addict" in 2002. In February 2002, Dior opened its first Dior Homme boutique in Milan. By 2002, 130 locations were operational. Until 2002, Kanebo held the ready-to-wear license in Japan, and after the license expired, Dior began selling ready-to-wear and accessories directly. The "Chris 47 Steel" watch was released in 2003 as a cousin to the "Chris 47 Aluminum." On 7 December 2003, Bernard Arnault, Hélène Mercier-Arnault, and Sidney Toledano witnessed the opening of the Dior flagship boutique in Tokyo's Omotesandō district. A second Dior flagship store opened in Tokyo's Ginza in 2004. An exclusive Dior Homme boutique opened in Paris on Rue Royale that year, presenting the full Dior Homme collection. A second Dior Fine Jewelry boutique opened at 8 Place Vendôme. A Christian Dior boutique opened in Moscow after the company took control of its licensed operations there. Victoire de Castellane launched her watch "Le D de Dior," designed for women but incorporating masculine design elements. Slimane then launched the "Chiffre Rouge" watch for Dior Homme, emphasizing the integration of watch design and technology to reflect Dior Homme's artistic excellence. De Castellane launched a second watch line, "La Baby de Dior," with a more feminine, jewelry-inspired design. In 2005, the "Miss Dior Chérie" and "Dior Homme" fragrances were released. Galliano launched the "Dior Christal" watches, combining steel and blue sapphires. In 2005, Christian Dior S.A. celebrated the 13th anniversary of Dior Watches, and the "Chiffre Rouge" collection was recognized by the World Watches and Jewelry Show in Basel, Switzerland. The same year, the fashion house celebrated the 100th anniversary of Christian Dior's birth. An exhibition, "Christian Dior: Man of the Century," was held at the Dior Museum in Granville, Normandy. In 2006, the Dior watch booth featured the Dior Canework pattern, designed by Christian Dior and based on Napoleon III chairs used in his fashion shows. In 2007, Kris Van Assche was appointed artistic director of Dior Homme and presented his first collection that year. The 60th anniversary of the Maison Dior was officially celebrated in 2007. By February 2011, Dior faced a scandal after accusations of John Galliano making antisemitic remarks, leading to a "public relations nightmare." Galliano was fired in March, and the Fall-Winter 2011/2012 collection was presented without him on 4 March. Before the show, CEO Sidney Toledano delivered a speech on Christian Dior's values and its ties to the Holocaust. The show ended with atelier staff receiving applause in Galliano's absence. Bill Gaytten was appointed interim head designer. His first haute-couture collection for the Fall-Winter 2011 season was presented in July and received mainly negative reviews. During the 13-month period without an artistic director, Dior's designs gradually shifted away from Galliano's theatrical style. The redesigned dior.com launched in late 2011. Raf Simons was announced on 11 April 2012 as the new artistic director, known for his minimalist designs, contrasting with Galliano's dramatic style. The company emphasized Simons' connection to Christian Dior, comparing him to the original designer. Simons spent time in the Dior archives and studied haute-couture, having no prior experience in the field. His first collection, the Fall-Winter 2012 haute-couture line, was presented on 2 July and was hailed as "the new couture," marking a fresh start for Dior. The collection referenced Christian Dior's post-World War II designs and made more references to the original designer than to the house itself. Simons' work was described as wiping the haute-couture slate clean. He gave an interview published through Dior Mag. While previous Galliano shows were held at the Musée Rodin, Simons' show was held at a different venue. Gaytten's Spring-Summer 2012 haute-couture collection was presented in Shanghai on 14 April, marking the first Dior haute-couture show in China and the last under Gaytten's leadership. He remained head designer for the John Galliano label. On 3 May, the Dior: Secret Garden — Versailles promotional film was launched, highlighting the brand's transition. Simons' Fall-Winter 2012 collection was recognized as a major highlight of the season.

On 3 May, the promotional film Dior: Secret Garden — Versailles was launched, generating significant buzz across industry and social media as a representation of Dior’s transformation. On 2 July, Kim Jones presented his first collection for the house, the Fall-Winter 2012 haute-couture collection, which was hailed as "the new couture" and marked a fresh start under Simons, who was described as wiping the haute couture slate clean. The collection made more references to Mr. Dior than to the house of Dior, echoing post-World War II design themes. Simons, who rarely gives interviews, participated in a Dior Mag online feature. Unlike previous Galliano shows held at the Musée Rodin, Simons’ presentation took place at a private residence near the Arc de Triomphe, with the address shared only with select clients, celebrities, journalists, and staff. Attendees included Azzedine Alaïa, Pierre Cardin, Alber Elbaz, Diane von Fürstenberg, Marc Jacobs, Christopher Kane, Olivier Theyskens, Riccardo Tisci, Donatella Versace, Princess Charlene of Monaco, actresses Marion Cotillard, Mélanie Laurent, Jennifer Lawrence, Sharon Stone, film producer Harvey Weinstein, and Dior chairman Arnault with his daughter. A live satellite feed was available on DiorMag, and Twitter was used for real-time updates. Prior to this, Dior had acquired the Parisian embroidery firm Maison Vermont in early 2012. In March 2014, Peter Philips was appointed as Dior’s new creative and image director for makeup, replacing Pat McGrath. In March 2015, Rihanna was named the official spokeswoman, becoming the first Black woman to hold the role. In 2015, Israeli model Sofia Mechetner was chosen as Dior’s new face. In 2016, Maria Grazia Chiuri was named women’s artistic director. In April 2016, a new Dior flagship boutique opened in San Francisco, hosted by Jaime King. In 2017, Dior renovated and expanded its Madrid store, celebrating the opening with a masked ball attended by Spanish celebrities including Alejandro Gómez Palomo. In March 2018, Kim Jones was named men’s artistic director, leading several high-profile streetwear collaborations, including with Brian Donnelly (KAWS), Raymond Pettibon, 1017 ALYX 9SM, Yoon Ahn, Hajime Sorayama, Daniel Arsham, Sacai, and Shawn Stussy. In October 2019, Dior apologized to China for using a map of China that excluded Taiwan. In October 2021, Francis Kurkdjian was appointed creative director of Dior perfume. On 11 March 2022, 30 Avenue Montaigne reopened to the public after a two-year renovation led by architect Peter Marino; historically, this location hosted Christian Dior’s first collection. In January 2023, Delphine Arnault was named chairperson and CEO, beginning in February. On 6 August 2025, Dior Spa New York opened in Manhattan, located on the top floor of the renovated House of Dior flagship at Madison Avenue and 57th Street, designed by Peter Marino and scented with a custom fragrance by Francis Kurkdjian. In June 2024, Manufactures Dior SRL was placed in judicial administration in Italy after being accused of subcontracting work to Chinese equity firms that mistreated employees. In 2025, Jonathan Anderson was appointed as Dior’s new Creative Director for women’s, men’s, and haute couture collections, succeeding Kim Jones and Maria Grazia Chiuri. Dior pays subcontractors as little as 53 euros for a handbag sold for 2600 euros. In 2000, Galliano’s collection inspired by homeless people drew criticism and attention. In early 2011, Galliano was accused of making antisemitic comments after drinking in Paris, stating “I love Hitler” and “People like you would be dead today,” which is illegal in France and punishable by up to six months in prison; on 1 March 2011, Christian Dior officially fired Galliano. In 2017, Dior faced accusations of cultural appropriation for copying a traditional Romanian vest, the Bihor coat, using the same colors and patterns in its pre-fall collection without credit; Romanian fashion magazine Beau Monde launched a campaign, recruiting native craftsmen and designers from Bihor to create authentic versions, and launched the online platform Bihor Couture to publicly shame Dior and sell original designs. In April 2022, Dior released a new midi-skirt in Seoul, designed by Maria Grazia Chiuri as a tribute to Catherine Dior, featuring a plain black wrap-around skirt with two panels, four flat panels, pleats, and overlapping construction, described as a modern variation of a hallmark Dior silhouette. Three months later, Hanfu enthusiasts criticized the skirt for copying the mamianqun design, noting its identical cut and construction to the Ming dynasty (1368–1644 AD) version, though Chinese netizens pointed out that modern midi-mamianqun designs had been created by Hanfu designers. Dior halted sales of the skirt in Mainland China to avoid controversy. On 23 July, about 50 Chinese overseas students in Paris protested in front of a Dior flagship store at the Champs-Élysées with the slogans “Dior, Stop Cultural Appropriation” and “This is a traditional Chinese dress,” calling for international student solidarity and receiving support from the Communist Youth League of China; over 10 Chinese democratic activists also participated with banners such as “Skirt Rights Is Bigger Than Human Rights,” sparking conflict. Chinese media initially focused on the cultural appropriation accusation without covering the anti-protest. Some French media, including Journal du Luxe, argued that the core issue was Dior’s lack of transparency about the origins of the skirt’s design, not the design itself; Chinese netizens criticized Dior on Weibo with comments like “Was Dior inspired by Taobao?” and an Instagram user wrote: “Taking cultural references from our country [China] is more than welcomed; however, this does not mean that you can appropriate our culture and deny the fact that this skirt is Chinese!” In July 2022, Dior faced further accusations for using a huaniaotu (bird-and-flower painting) pattern, a traditional Chinese theme from the Tang dynasty, in its 2022 Autumn Winter ready-to-wear collection, which it presented as its signature motif Jardin d'Hiver, inspired by Christian Dior’s wall murals. In June 2024, Italian authorities placed Manufactures Dior SRL under judicial administration for one year due to poor labor practices, including exploitative conditions for 32 workers, two of whom were undocumented immigrants and seven lacking proper documentation, living and working in unsanitary conditions with inadequate safety measures and machinery safety devices removed to increase production. In July 2024, the Autorità Garante della Concorrenza e del Mercato (AGCM) launched an investigation into Dior and other fashion companies to determine if they misled consumers about labor practices and supply chain management. In May 2025, Dior confirmed a cyberattack resulting in a data breach that compromised personal customer information, primarily in China, discovered on 7 May, including names, gender, email, postal addresses, phone numbers, and purchase history. In early July, Dior faced backlash for a $200,000 coat from Jonathan Anderson’s debut collection featuring mukaish, a traditional Indian embroidery technique, with fashion commentator Hanan Besnovic highlighting the lack of credit to Indian artisans, echoing the Prada Kolhapuri chappals controversy. At the end of 2010, Groupe Arnault SAS was the only major shareholder in Christian Dior S.A., holding 69.96% of shares and 82.86% of voting rights; Christian Dior S.A. held 42.36% of LVMH shares and 59.01% of its voting rights, with Arnault holding an additional 5.28% of shares and 4.65% of votes. As of April 2023, the company operates 535 locations.
